args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the latest deploy of v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The service was unhealthy with an 18% error rate. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before it went to production. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and review why a release candidate that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

**Rollback**
- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Version chosen:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production.
- **After:** all three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is 0.2%.
- No approval was needed, since v2.3.0 has already been healthy in production.

**Incident INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api)**
- The incident is open and the on-call engineer has been paged.
- It describes the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback to v2.3.0 and the recovery numbers.
- It also notes that the test build for v2.3.1 was already failing in staging, but the release still went to production. That's worth looking into along with the root cause.
- My first attempt to create it timed out. I checked that nothing had been created, then retried with a unique key that prevents duplicates, so there's only one incident and one page.
